data_provenance: synthetic crew data; vitamin storage losses from first-order kinetics anchored to published spaceflight-food retention data; physiology parameters from NASA/literature sources where available, otherwise assumed (see parameter_sources and /api/v1/health/parameters)

scenario_preset.label: Major storage failure
scenario_preset.description: At Sol 150 the food-storage cooling fails for 60 Sols and peaks at 30 °C; the greenhouse goes offline. This is the mildest failure (searched over 60-240 Sols x 30-45 °C) in which an astronaut's vitamin B1 body store actually falls below its risk threshold.

status_rules.ACT: forecast Sols-to-risk <= 45 (vitamin C, B1 pools or vitamin D status)
status_rules.WATCH: forecast Sols-to-risk <= 120 or |z| of any vital >= 2.0 (vs a trend-following personal reference lagged 28 Sols)
status_rules.driver: largest contributor relative to its rule threshold: 120 / Sols-to-risk (nutrient forecast) vs |z| / 2.0 (vital); ACT is always forecast-driven
status_rules.CALIBRATING: personal baseline + trend window not yet available

vitamin_d_meta.label: Vitamin D (25-OH-D)
vitamin_d_meta.model: 25-OH-D declines exponentially (no UV in flight); rate scales with intake shortfall vs 25 ug/day
